Modeled: the parallel write (address A2-A0, data AN2 AN1 BD3-BD0 latched on the rising edge of CS), the Code B decode, 1:3 triplexed backplane drive at 90 Hz, VDISP high = shutdown (pins released, data kept). Not modeled: VDISP open = shutdown, the display voltage levels, the CS mid-level test mode, the oscillator, power-up latch contents (reset to dark).

engineNeeds.need: MAX7233 / MAX7234 18-segment ASCII decode (a DATA need, not an engine need)
engineNeeds.semantics: With a table, the devices are the same shape as these: one 18-bit register per character (3 backplanes x 6 segment lines U V W X Y Z) and one command per (address, 6-bit code) that sets it to a constant (64 codes x 4 or 5 characters x 2 fonts). The table needs, for each code (code = ASCII & 0x3F: D5 D4 = 00 @ A-O, 01 P-Z [ \ ] ^ _, 10 space ! " # $ % & ' ( ) * + , - . /, 11 0-9 : ; < = > ?) the lit (line, COM) cells; max7231-max7234 p.12 Table 3 shows the glyphs (A suffix half-width digits, B full-width) and p.13 Figure 20 the segment-to-cell wiring; both are low-resolution scans that could not be read to cell level without guessing. Parallel 7233: CS1 and CS2 both low then the rising edge of either latches (bus cs = CS1, wr = CS2 works); serial 7234: 9 bits D0 first, then A0 A1 A2 (align end, as the 7232), tenth clock resets.
engineNeeds.neededBy: MAX7233AFIPL/BFIPL, MAX7234AFIPL/BFIPL (+ FIQ), none in stock at DigiKey on 2026-11-23

engineNeeds.need: DATA ACCEPTED output (ICM7232, MAX7232, MAX7234 pin 37)
engineNeeds.semantics: An output driven by the serial bit count of the current transfer, beside the `lcd` display driver (a device has one display driver): high after power-up and after every WRITE pulse; low once 8 DATA CLOCK rising edges have been counted since the last WRITE pulse (ICM7232 / MAX7232: stays low for the 9th and 10th, goes high again at the 11th, which also resets the shift register; MAX7234: low after the 9th, high at the 10th). An `output` pin never driven today.

With `align: "end"` the engine matches the last bits before the transaction ends however many were clocked. The chips discard a word whose 11th clock arrived (reset of the shift register and control logic): an optional protocol key such as `maxBits` (a transaction with more bits matches no command) would model it. Today a word of 11 or more bits writes its last 10 bits.

engineNeeds.need: open input as a level for pins.levels
engineNeeds.semantics: VDISP open (or within 1 V of V+) = shutdown (harris p.6, max p.4). `pins.levels` reads a floating (Z) pin as 0, so an unconnected VDISP is not shutdown here; only a pin driven to 1 is. A `levels` entry form that copies Z as a third value (or as 1) would model the open pin.

engineNeeds.need: optional: serial commit on the WRITE rising edge
engineNeeds.semantics: The engine commits an active-high-selected SPI frame when the select falls (the start of the active-low WRITE pulse); the chip decodes on the pulse's rising edge, up to 500 ns later. Not host-visible at the bench's time scale.

notes: Ten devices in lcddriver.json, 21 parts: ICM7231 (BFIJL ceramic, BFIPL), ICM7232A (AFIJL ceramic, AFIPL), ICM7232B (BFIPL), ICM7232C (CRIPL, reversed pinout), MAX7231A/B/C and MAX7232A/B/C (sheet names ...FIPL and ...FIQ, plus the DigiKey names MAX7231BFIPL+, MAX7231BFIQH+D, MAX7231CFIPL+). Footprints PDIP-40-600, CDIP-40-600, PLCC-44 exist (no missingFootprints). Modeled with the `lcd` driver 1:3 (main engine, no patch needed): 9-bit RAM register per digit (bit 3 x line + backplane, line Z=0 Y=1 X=2), the font decode as constants set by the bus commands (128 commands for the parallel devices, 480 for the serial ones), parallel write on the rising edge of CS (bus wr = CS), serial 8/9/10-bit words (spi, cs = WRITE active high, align end), 5556 us frame (90 Hz typ, p.5 / p.3), VDISP = 1 shutdown. The Harris sheet has no maker-hosted copy (renesas.com/en/document/dst/icm7231-datasheet, icm7232-datasheet, analog.com ICM7232.pdf all 404; web search finds only third-party copies and Renesas AN054): the ICM parts take no datasheet key. max7231-max7234 URL (analog.com MAX7231-MAX7234.pdf) answers with a PDF byte-identical in size (640616) to the local file. max7231-max7234-maxim-old is the SAME 1995 sheet re-scanned in 2001 (same pages, same text): both ids carry the same URL; the main thread may drop the old PDF. Unresolved: A/B annunciator assignment (Table 3 / Table 1 pictures versus Figure 13 and pin labels; see spec section 5), the model follows the pin labels. The bundled GENERIC-LCD-8D-1:3 glass groups its cells (A F E / B G D / C DP) differently from these chips (b c an1 / a g d / f e an2 per line), so wired line-for-line it lights cells that are not the digit's segments; the bench compares lit cells with the RAM bits through that grouping. A purpose-made glass (3 pins per digit: B C DP, A G D, F E) would show the fonts, with the annunciators and the C layout needing their own cell names; not added (glass is not this letter's kind). Bench icm7231_max7231_test.c (212 checks): add logic_test(icm7231_max7231_test) after display_out_test in backend/CMakeLists.txt. In the scratch build (main + max695x-display.patch + pcf8576-lcd-mode-after-max695x.patch) every test passes except listing_check and trace_check, which differ only by the 21 new parts (additions: regenerate parts.txt / traces.txt).
